children: Georgia Power unit said Monday it signed ​an agreement with Google
at two of its nuclear plants that could allow the facilities to add ~96 MW of new capacity to the electric grid to serve the utility's customers.
The agreement, which is subject to approval from the Georgia Public Service Commission, ​would fund power uprates at ​Georgia Power's share of the Vogtle and Hatch ‌nuclear ⁠units.

Georgia Power said it filed documents with the Georgia PSC that include a new nuclear uprate tariff structure and a request to approve an extended power uprate for Plant Hatch 1 & 2, while an EPU for Plant Vogtle 1 & 2 was previously approved by the PSC in the 2025 integrated resource plan.

"We appreciate Google's continued leadership in this space and partnership in developing this program, which we see as the latest example of how large-load growth can benefit all electric customers," Georgia Power Senior VP of Strategic Growth Aaron Mitchell said.
